newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah plunges in late trading.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah plunges in late trading.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah plunged against the dollar in late trading on Friday due to regional spillovers and short-covering ahead of the weekend.
Spot rupiah broke through the psychological level of 2,500 rupiah at 0840 GMT from an opening of 2,472/75.
The rupiah hovered in the range between 2,470 and 2,480 in the morning before offshore operators pushed the it through several support levels which triggered stop-loss covering.
"I don't think it has much to do with fundamentals. This is now purely speculation," one dealer in Singapore said.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,505/10 at 0945 GMT. Dealers said the low of the day for the rupiah was 2,510 to the dollar.

Dealers said spillover from the region was mainly responsible for the rupiah's fall. Regional currencies racked up further losses as funds continued to pile into the U.S. dollar as nervousness in the region continued, dealers said.
They said liquidity remained very low and spreads wide, exaggerating currency movements.
One U.S. bank dealer said volume was a bit thin because many players had stayed out of the volatile market, enabling speculators to dictate the market with a few million dollars.

The rupiah has been on the declines since the de facto devaluations of the Thai baht and Philippine peso earlier this month, forcing Bank Indonesia to take a pre-emptive move to widen the dollar-rupiah intervention band.
Dealers said it was anticipated that the rupiah could fall through the 2,500 support level after the London market opened.
"It's not a surprise to us. The rupiah is bound to fall through this level. If not in the morning, then during London time or at latest when the U.S. market opens," one dealer said.
Dealers said some offshore players had been seen trying to push the dollar through the 2,500 level since the morning, but met resistance from a mixture of local and foreign players.

They said forward rates were not rattled much but were trending higher, in line with the weakening rupiah. They said offshore players had increased swap holdings previously to prepare for a possible squeeze by the central bank.
However, the central bank kept its money policy unchanged.
Dealers said the rupiah was driven into another wave of turbulence following offshore attacks on the Malaysia ringgit and the Singapore dollar.
"Even the Singapore dollars came under pressure. So you can expect something on the rupiah," one dealer said.
He said the Singapore dollar had been driven into the hot zone which concerned some operators about the fate of other regional currencies, including the rupiah.
The dealer said stop-loss and weekend covering and relatively large corporate demand seemed to have added up to the rupiah's woe on Friday.
Dealers said corporate demand for dollars was a bit high, causing overnight dollar to rise to seven percent from the usual rates of around 5.75 percent.
One local bank dealer said money market liquidity was also volatile on Friday, with overnight money rising to a high of 19 percent from 13.0 percent, but later falling to eight percent.
"The market in the region is still volatile and nervous. I think it could continue for some time before things can cool down. It depends all on the region," another dealer said.
He said further volatility was expected next week.
Overnight swap was at 0.35/0.45 and tom.next at 0.15/0.17.
One-month swap was at 17,5/19.0, two at 35.0/40.0, three at 57.0/60.0 and six at 113.0/117.0 points.

The central bank kept its intervention band at 2,377/2,681 but raised its conversion band to 2,465/2,513 on Friday from 2,437/2,485 on Wednesday. All markets were closed on Thursday for a public holiday. -- Jakarta newsroom +6221 384-6364
